headline: Audit and inference design choices alter conclusions in biomedical ML evaluation
label: Evaluation Design In Biomedical Inference
summary: Recent preprints show that persistence rules, ablation tests, reference pinning, and provenance audits each shift biomedical model conclusions.
synthesis: Across these four preprints, the dominant thread is that the design of an evaluation, rather than the model alone, governs the conclusions drawn in biomedical inference. BioAgent-DF audits biomedical research agents by swapping saved computation values to separate evidence use from final verdicts. A design-based analysis shows that action-ablation diagnostics in biological world models can falsely report action effects under autocorrelated designs, and proposes a finite-sample test. TARE pins database-size settings so unchanged Pfam, HMMER, and Infernal searches can be replayed across reference releases, or refused. A permutation-calibrated estimator addresses persistence rules that misdate probe onsets under depth correlation, tested on co-folding models. What is new is explicit attribution of inferential errors to specific mechanisms: decision provenance, ablation confounds, reference-release dependence, and temporal correlation. This framing is dominant rather than universal across the items.
